inputs.instruction:
Please convert this command to run for the Slurm Workload manager.
The cluster will have the Elastic Fabric Adapter for low latency networking, running on hpc7g.6xlarge.
These details have no implications for the Slurm directives, they are for your FYI.

Since we are converting to Slurm (with more flags and options) you MUST try to write the command to IMPROVE performance.
Please add comments to the sbatch script about what you did and why.
Here are directives for Slurm:
Usage: sbatch [OPTIONS(0)...] [ : [OPTIONS(N)...]] script(0) [args(0)...]

Parallel run options:
  -a, --array=indexes         job array index values
  -A, --account=name          charge job to specified account
      --bb=<spec>             burst buffer specifications
      --bbf=<file_name>       burst buffer specification file
  -b, --begin=time            defer job until HH:MM MM/DD/YY
      --comment=name          arbitrary comment
      --cpu-freq=min[-max[:gov]] requested cpu frequency (and governor)
  -c, --cpus-per-task=ncpus   number of cpus required per task
  -d, --dependency=type:jobid[:time] defer job until condition on jobid is satisfied
      --deadline=time         remove the job if no ending possible before
                              this deadline (start > (deadline - time[-min]))
      --delay-boot=mins       delay boot for desired node features
  -D, --chdir=directory       set working directory for batch script
  -e, --error=err             file for batch script's standard error
      --export[=names]        specify environment variables to export
      --export-file=file|fd   specify environment variables file or file
                              descriptor to export
      --get-user-env          load environment from local cluster
      --gid=group_id          group ID to run job as (user root only)
      --gres=list             required generic resources per node
      --gres-flags=opts       flags related to GRES management
  -H, --hold                  submit job in held state
      --ignore-pbs            Ignore #PBS and #BSUB options in the batch script
  -i, --input=in              file for batch script's standard input
  -J, --job-name=jobname      name of job
  -k, --no-kill               do not kill job on node failure
  -L, --licenses=names        required license, comma separated
  -M, --clusters=names        Comma separated list of clusters to issue
                              commands to.  Default is current cluster.
                              Name of 'all' will submit to run on all clusters.
                              NOTE: SlurmDBD must up.
      --container             Path to OCI container bundle
      --container-id          OCI container ID
  -m, --distribution=type     distribution method for processes to nodes
                              (type = block|cyclic|arbitrary)
      --mail-type=type        notify on state change: BEGIN, END, FAIL or ALL
      --mail-user=user        who to send email notification for job state
                              changes
      --mcs-label=mcs         mcs label if mcs plugin mcs/group is used
  -n, --ntasks=ntasks         number of tasks to run
      --nice[=value]          decrease scheduling priority by value
      --no-requeue            if set, do not permit the job to be requeued
      --ntasks-per-node=n     number of tasks to invoke on each node
  -N, --nodes=N               number of nodes on which to run (N = min[-max])
      --oom-kill-step[=0|1]   set the OOMKillStep behaviour
  -o, --output=out            file for batch script's standard output
  -O, --overcommit            overcommit resources
  -p, --partition=partition   partition requested
      --parsable              outputs only the jobid and cluster name (if present),
                              separated by semicolon, only on successful submission.
      --power=flags           power management options
      --priority=value        set the priority of the job to value
      --profile=value         enable acct_gather_profile for detailed data
                              value is all or none or any combination of
                              energy, lustre, network or task
      --propagate[=rlimits]   propagate all [or specific list of] rlimits
  -q, --qos=qos               quality of service
  -Q, --quiet                 quiet mode (suppress informational messages)
      --reboot                reboot compute nodes before starting job
      --requeue[=expedited]   if set, permit the job to be requeued
  -s, --oversubscribe         over subscribe resources with other jobs
  -S, --core-spec=cores       count of reserved cores
      --signal=[[R][B]:]num[@time] send signal when time limit within time seconds
      --spread-job            spread job across as many nodes as possible
      --spread-segments       spread job segments across separate base blocks
      --switches=max-switches{@max-time-to-wait}
                              Optimum switches and max time to wait for optimum
      --thread-spec=threads   count of reserved threads
  -t, --time=minutes          time limit
      --time-min=minutes      minimum time limit (if distinct)
      --tres-bind=...         task to tres binding options
      --tres-per-task=list    list of tres required per task
      --uid=user_id           user ID to run job as (user root only)
      --use-min-nodes         if a range of node counts is given, prefer the
                              smaller count
  -v, --verbose               verbose mode (multiple -v's increase verbosity)
  -W, --wait                  wait for completion of submitted job
      --wckey=wckey           wckey to run job under
      --wrap[=command string] wrap command string in a sh script and submit

Constraint options:
      --cluster-constraint=[!]list specify a list of cluster constraints
      --contiguous            demand a contiguous range of nodes
  -C, --constraint=list       specify a list of constraints
  -F, --nodefile=filename     request a specific list of hosts
      --mem=MB                minimum amount of real memory
      --mincpus=n             minimum number of logical processors (threads)
                              per node
      --reservation=name      allocate resources from named reservation
      --tmp=MB                minimum amount of temporary disk
  -w, --nodelist=hosts...     request a specific list of hosts
  -x, --exclude=hosts...      exclude a specific list of hosts

Consumable resources related options:
      --exclusive[=user]      allocate nodes in exclusive mode when
                              cpu consumable resource is enabled
      --exclusive[=mcs]       allocate nodes in exclusive mode when
                              cpu consumable resource is enabled
                              and mcs plugin is enabled
      --mem-per-cpu=MB        maximum amount of real memory per allocated
                              cpu required by the job.
                              --mem >= --mem-per-cpu if --mem is specified.
      --resv-ports            reserve communication ports

Affinity/Multi-core options: (when the task/affinity plugin is enabled)
                              For the following 4 options, you are
                              specifying the minimum resources available for
                              the node(s) allocated to the job.
      --sockets-per-node=S    number of sockets per node to allocate
      --cores-per-socket=C    number of cores per socket to allocate
      --threads-per-core=T    number of threads per core to allocate
  -B, --extra-node-info=S[:C[:T]]  combine request of sockets per node,
                              cores per socket and threads per core.
                              Specify an asterisk (*) as a placeholder,
                              a minimum value, or a min-max range.

      --ntasks-per-core=n     number of tasks to invoke on each core
      --ntasks-per-socket=n   number of tasks to invoke on each socket
      --hint=                 Bind tasks according to application hints
                              (see "--hint=help" for options)
      --mem-bind=             Bind memory to locality domains (ldom)
                              (see "--mem-bind=help" for options)

GPU scheduling options:
      --cpus-per-gpu=n        number of CPUs required per allocated GPU
  -G, --gpus=n                count of GPUs required for the job
      --gpu-bind=...          task to gpu binding options
      --gpu-freq=...          frequency and voltage of GPUs
      --gpus-per-node=n       number of GPUs required per allocated node
      --gpus-per-socket=n     number of GPUs required per allocated socket
      --gpus-per-task=n       number of GPUs required per spawned task
      --mem-per-gpu=n         real memory required per allocated GPU

Help options:
  -h, --help                  show this help message
      --usage                 display brief usage message

Other options:
  -V, --version               output version information and exit

You must NOT load any modules, as all software is active.
You MUSt add --mpi=pmix to all Slurm (e.g., srun) commands as we require it.
The user will not be able to edit your generated script - it MUST be in final form.

All applications are on the path except for:

 osu-all-reduce: /usr/local/libexec/osu-micro-benchmarks/mpi/collective/osu_allreduce
osu-latency: /usr/local/libexec/osu-micro-benchmarks/mpi/pt2pt/osu_latency

Add echo "Start time:" $( date +%s ) before your running command
Add echo "End time:" $( date +%s ) after your running command
inputs.script: flux submit -N1 -n 64 lmp -v x 20 -v y 20 -v z 20 -in in.reaxff.hns

outputs.summary: The flux command was successfully converted to a Slurm batch script. I have translated the node and task counts, and added performance-enhancing directives such as exclusive node access and CPU binding, along with comments explaining each choice. The script also includes the required MPI flag and start/end time echoes.
outputs.implications: The original request of 64 tasks on a single node (-N1 -n64) is preserved. However, the specified 'hpc7g.6xlarge' instance has only 24 physical cores. Running 64 tasks will result in significant oversubscription of the CPU cores, which will likely degrade application performance due to context switching. The performance improvements added (--exclusive, --cpu-bind) are best practices but may not overcome the negative impact of this oversubscription.
outputs.jobspec:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
#
# Slurm batch script for a LAMMPS simulation
#

# -- Job Details --
# It is good practice to name your job and specify output/error files
#SBATCH --job-name=lammps_simulation
#SBATCH --output=lammps_simulation_%j.out
#SBATCH --error=lammps_simulation_%j.err

# -- Resource Allocation --
# Request 1 node, which is the direct translation of 'flux submit -N1'.
#SBATCH --nodes=1

# Request 64 total tasks, which is the direct translation of 'flux submit -n64'.
#SBATCH --ntasks=64

# Explicitly state that all 64 tasks should run on each node.
# This is redundant when --nodes=1 but adds clarity.
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=64

# -- Performance Enhancements --
# Request exclusive access to the node. This is crucial for performance
# as it prevents other jobs from running on the same node and causing
# resource contention (CPU, memory bandwidth, network).
#SBATCH --exclusive

# Bind tasks to specific cores. This improves performance by preventing the OS
# from migrating tasks between cores, which helps maintain CPU cache affinity.
#SBATCH --cpu-bind=cores


# -- Execution --
# Print the start time for job duration tracking
echo "Start time:" $( date +%s )

# Run the LAMMPS simulation using srun.
# The --mpi=pmix flag is added as required by the cluster configuration.
# srun will automatically use the resources allocated by the SBATCH directives above.
srun --mpi=pmix lmp -v x 20 -v y 20 -v z 20 -in in.reaxff.hns

# Print the end time for job duration tracking
echo "End time:" $( date +%s )
```

#!/bin/bash

#SBATCH -N 3
#SBATCH -n 192
#SBATCH --job-name=lammps_reaxff

# This directive ensures that tasks are evenly distributed across the nodes,
# with 64 tasks running on each of the 3 nodes. This can prevent imbalances
# that might degrade performance.

# It prevents other jobs from running on the same nodes, reducing contention
# for resources like CPU, memory, and network bandwidth, leading to more
# predictable and often better performance.

#SBATCH --cpu-bind=cores

srun --mpi=pmix lmp -v x 20 -v y 20 -v z 20 -in in.reaxff.hns

#!/bin/bash

# Set the job name
#SBATCH --job-name=lammps_hns

# Set the number of nodes
#SBATCH --nodes=5

# Set the total number of tasks (MPI processes)
#SBATCH --ntasks=320

# Set the number of tasks per node. This is calculated from total tasks / nodes (320/5=64).
# Explicitly setting this helps the scheduler allocate resources efficiently.
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=64

# Request exclusive access to the nodes.
# This is a key performance optimization that prevents other jobs from running on the same nodes,
# eliminating contention for CPU, memory, or network resources.
#SBATCH --exclusive

# Specify the distribution of tasks to nodes and CPUs.
# 'cyclic:cyclic' distributes tasks in a round-robin fashion across nodes, and then across CPUs within each node.
# This can improve performance for communication-bound applications by spreading MPI ranks and balancing network load.
#SBATCH --distribution=cyclic:cyclic

# Bind tasks to cores.
# This locks each MPI task to a specific CPU core, preventing the OS from migrating it.
# This improves cache performance and is critical for application stability and speed.
#SBATCH --cpu-bind=cores

# Specify the output and error files. %j will be replaced with the job ID.
#SBATCH --output=lmp_output_%j.out
#SBATCH --error=lmp_error_%j.err

# Start timing
echo "Start time:" $( date +%s )

# Run the parallel application using srun.
# The --mpi=pmix flag is explicitly requested for this cluster's MPI implementation.
srun --mpi=pmix lmp -v x 20 -v y 20 -v z 20 -in in.reaxff.hns

# End timing
echo "End time:" $( date +%s )

#!/bin/bash

#!/bin/bash

# Set the number of nodes for the job
#SBATCH --nodes=5

# Set the total number of tasks (MPI ranks)
#SBATCH --ntasks=320

# Set the number of tasks per node. This is calculated as ntasks/nodes (320/5 = 64)
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=64

# Set a name for the job, which will appear in queue listings
#SBATCH --job-name=lammps_simulation

# Specify the file for standard output. %j will be replaced with the job ID.
#SBATCH --output=lammps_output_%j.log

# Specify the file for standard error. %j will be replaced with the job ID.
#SBATCH --error=lammps_error_%j.log

# IMPROVE PERFORMANCE: Request exclusive access to the nodes.
# This prevents other jobs from running on the same nodes, reducing contention
# for shared resources like memory bandwidth and network interface.
#SBATCH --exclusive

# IMPROVE PERFORMANCE: Bind tasks to cores.
# This tells Slurm to pin each task to a specific CPU core, which can improve
# performance by increasing cache hits and reducing context switching.
# This is the analogous translation for flux's '-o cpu-affinity=per-task'.
#SBATCH --cpu-bind=cores

echo "Start time:" $( date +%s )

# Use srun to launch the parallel application.
# The --mpi=pmix flag is specified as required for the MPI implementation.
srun --mpi=pmix lmp -v x 20 -v y 20 -v z 20 -in in.reaxff.hns

echo "End time:" $( date +%s )

#!/bin/bash

# Set the job name for easier identification
#SBATCH --job-name=amg_job

# Specify the number of nodes required, equivalent to -N3 in the flux command.
#SBATCH --nodes=3

# Specify the total number of tasks (processes) to be launched, equivalent to -n 192 in flux.
#SBATCH --ntasks=192

# To improve performance, we explicitly define the number of tasks per node.
# This helps the scheduler with more efficient process placement.
# (192 total tasks / 3 nodes = 64 tasks per node)
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=64

# Request exclusive access to the nodes.
# This is a key performance improvement, as it ensures no other jobs can interfere
# with this job's access to resources like network or memory bandwidth.
#SBATCH --exclusive

# Define the files for standard output and error. Using %j inserts the job ID.
#SBATCH --output=amg_job_%j.out

#!/bin/bash

# Slurm job options

# --nodes=3: We are requesting 3 nodes, same as the -N3 in the flux command.
#SBATCH --nodes=3

# --ntasks=192: We are requesting 192 total tasks, same as the -n 192 in the flux command.
#SBATCH --ntasks=192

# --ntasks-per-node=64: For better resource allocation and performance, we explicitly
# state that we want 64 tasks per node (192 tasks / 3 nodes).
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=64

# --cpu-bind=cores: This binds each task to a specific CPU core. This is the equivalent
# of flux's cpu-affinity=per-task and can significantly improve performance by

#!/bin/bash

#SBATCH -N 1
# This requests one full node for the job.

#SBATCH -n 64
# This requests 64 tasks (MPI ranks) in total.

#SBATCH --exclusive
# This ensures the job has exclusive access to the node, preventing
# other jobs from running on it and potentially causing performance interference.
# This is a key optimization for tightly-coupled MPI applications.

#SBATCH --job-name=kripke_job
# Sets a descriptive name for the job in the queue.

#SBATCH --output=kripke_job.o%j
# Specifies the file for standard output, with the job ID (%j) appended.

#SBATCH --error=kripke_job.e%j

# --cpu-bind=cores: This is a performance optimization that pins each MPI task
# to a specific CPU core, which can improve performance by preventing process
# migration and improving cache utilization.
srun --mpi=pmix --cpu-bind=cores kripke --niter 100 --zones 64,64,64 --procs 4,4,4

echo "End time:" $( date +%s )

data.jobspec:
#!/bin/bash

#SBATCH -N 1
# This requests one full node for the job.

#SBATCH -n 64
# This requests 64 tasks (MPI ranks) in total.

#SBATCH --exclusive
# This ensures the job has exclusive access to the node, preventing
# other jobs from running on it and potentially causing performance interference.
# This is a key optimization for tightly-coupled MPI applications.

#SBATCH --job-name=kripke_job
# Sets a descriptive name for the job in the queue.

#SBATCH --output=kripke_job.o%j
# Specifies the file for standard output, with the job ID (%j) appended.

#SBATCH --error=kripke_job.e%j
# Specifies the file for standard error, with the job ID (%j) appended.

echo "Start time:" $( date +%s )

# srun is used to launch the parallel application.
# --mpi=pmix: Specifies the PMIx MPI type, as required.
# --cpu-bind=cores: This is a performance optimization that pins each MPI task
# to a specific CPU core, which can improve performance by preventing process
# migration and improving cache utilization.
srun --mpi=pmix --cpu-bind=cores kripke --niter 100 --zones 64,64,64 --procs 4,4,4

echo "End time:" $( date +%s )
